name: Ligny
summary: Napoleon fell on Blücher's Prussians strung out along the Ligny brook. All afternoon the villages of Saint-Amand and Ligny changed hands; in the evening the Imperial Guard broke the Prussian centre. Blücher, ridden over in a cavalry charge, survived, and his army fell back north towards Wavre in good order.

forces.name: Lefol's Division
forces.summary: Opened Vandamme's attack on Saint-Amand, fighting through the village and its walled orchards against Steinmetz's Prussians in some of the hardest fighting of the day.
notes: The 15e Léger brought three battalions, one more Light battalion than the list's one in four allows, which shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Berthezène's Division
forces.summary: Vandamme's reserve division, fed into the fighting around Saint-Amand as the Prussians counter-attacked through the afternoon.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Habert's Division
forces.summary: Fought on Vandamme's left around Saint-Amand-la-Haye and Wagnelée, where Blücher tried to turn the French flank.
notes: The 2e Régiment Étranger (Swiss) also served in Dupeyroux's brigade; the order of battle gives no battalion count, so it's left out.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Girard's Division
forces.summary: Lent from Reille's corps, it took Saint-Amand-la-Haye and held it against repeated Prussian attacks. Girard was mortally wounded leading it.
notes: Girard's division had five Light battalions (11e and 12e Léger) of eight, where the list allows one in four, so the extra Light battalions show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Pécheux's Division
forces.summary: Gérard's leading division against Ligny itself, where the fight for the village and its churchyard went on for hours at close quarters.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Vichery's Division
forces.summary: Fed into Ligny village behind Pécheux, and part of the final push when the Guard broke through in the evening.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Hulot's Division
forces.summary: Led by Hulot after Bourmont deserted the day before, it held Gérard's right towards Tongrinne against Thielemann's corps.
notes: Bourmont commanded the division until he deserted to the allies on 15 June; Hulot led it from then. The order of battle gives the division no battery of its own; one foot battery is shown.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: The Middle Guard
forces.formation: 3rd and 4th Grenadiers and Chasseurs à Pied
forces.summary: The Guard's grenadiers and chasseurs, sent in at dusk through Ligny village, broke the Prussian centre and decided the battle.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Delort's Cuirassiers
forces.summary: Milhaud's cuirassiers followed the Guard through the Prussian centre at dusk and caught Blücher's last counter-charge, in which the old marshal was unhorsed.
notes: A cavalry division on its own has no Infantry Brigade, which the list needs; its cavalry brigades are allowed by infantry brigades, and reserve cavalry can be at most half an army. So these show as historical departures. Play it alongside an infantry division, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Zieten's I Corps
forces.formation: I Corps, Army of the Lower Rhine
forces.summary: Held the line of the Ligny brook from Saint-Amand to Ligny itself, and bore the worst of the day: Steinmetz's brigade fought for Saint-Amand all afternoon, Jagow's and Henckel's held Ligny village house by house until the Guard broke through at dusk.
notes: The order of battle gives Pirch II's brigade four regiments, the 16th Infantry among them, where the list's brigade has at most two Line regiments and three in all, so these show as historical departures.
A Prussian brigade was the size of another army's division, so the whole corps is here. Take the brigades you want; each is a force in itself.

Each regiment's three battalions are the list's two Musketeer and one Fusilier battalions, or three Landwehr. The corps' cavalry and reserve artillery aren't included, and the order of battle doesn't number the brigades' foot batteries.
Zieten is the book's named commander.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named General Hans Ernst Karl, Graf von Zieten, with his own rating.

forces.name: Pirch's II Corps
forces.formation: II Corps, Army of the Lower Rhine
forces.summary: Blücher's reserve behind the line, fed in brigade by brigade: into Saint-Amand-la-Haye and Wagnelée to try to turn the French left, and into Ligny as the centre was worn down.
notes: A Prussian brigade was the size of another army's division, so the whole corps is here. Take the brigades you want; each is a force in itself.

forces.name: Thielemann's III Corps
forces.formation: III Corps, Army of the Lower Rhine
forces.summary: Held the Prussian left around Sombreffe, Tongrinne and Boignée. Kept apart from the main fight by Grouchy's cavalry and Hulot's division, it came through the day the least hurt of Blücher's corps.
notes: Luck's brigade was all Landwehr, two Kurmark regiments, where the list's brigade needs a Line regiment, which shows as a historical departure.
